name: Deckers Outdoor Corporation
moat_justification: Two premium brands (HOKA, UGG) with proven pricing power — gross margin expanded from 50.3% in FY2023 to 57.7-57.9% in FY2025-26 on full-price selling and disciplined distribution — and returns on invested capital far above the cost of capital for five years, but footwear has no switching costs, both brands are fashion-exposed, and HOKA faces On, Nike and Brooks in its own category.
fragility_flags: BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.1%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (11.9%) vs bull-case tier B (18.8%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Premium two-brand footwear compounder, moat 6/10 — just clears 15% on the TTM base (15.4% weighted, IV $88.55 vs $85.71) with the verdict sized to the bear end (Tier C at 11.9%); it clears 15% only below $88.55, so there is almost no margin of safety at the current price.
moat_for: HOKA and UGG brand strength with proven pricing power: gross margin 50.3% (FY2023) to 57.9% (FY2025) and 57.7% (FY2026), TTM 57.8%, on full-price selling

Returns on invested capital far above the cost of capital through the last five fiscal years (roic_proxy in fundamentals.json; the level is flattered by the tiny asset-light capital base, the direction is not in doubt)
Distribution discipline: selective wholesale, controlled inventory (Q1 FY27 inventory down 5% YoY) and a growing DTC channel (+13% in Q1 FY27) protect full-price realization
Asset-light model with a fortress balance sheet: $1.91B cash at FY2026 year-end, no outstanding borrowings, funding a buyback that shrank the diluted count 3.1%/yr
International runway: international was 41.7% of FY2026 sales and is growing faster than domestic (+8.4% vs +3.2% in Q1 FY27)
moat_against: No switching costs — consumer footwear loyalty is fashion-driven and revocable; UGG has faded before (FY2017 operating income was negative in the filed history)
HOKA competition is intensifying in its own niche: On Holding growing far faster in premium running, Nike fighting to retake shelf space, Brooks entrenched in stability
Two-brand concentration: HOKA plus UGG are essentially the whole company; the other-brands segment shrank 18.1% in Q1 FY27

Sourcing concentration in Vietnam / Southeast Asia — tariff headwind was guided at roughly $150M unmitigated for FY2026, and FY2027 gross-margin guidance (~56.5%) already embeds tariff and freight pressure
Growth has decelerated hard: revenue +16.5% 5-yr CAGR to +9.8% in FY2026, +5.7% in Q1 FY27, with FY2027 guided at +7-8%
